newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mostly lower on early origin selling activity. Bench mark March closed $2 down on the day at $1,227 per tonne. Spot January was $7 off at $1,250 per tonne. News that Ugandan coffee sales in December were significantly up had a slightly negative impact. In New York arabica futures closed lower across the board. March gave up 40 points to close at 116.25 cents/lb, while May ended 60 points lower at 114.35 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 0.25 to 1.25 cents/lb. There were no fresh news to influence prices.

UGANDA - According to the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) coffee exports in December 1996 reached 985,403 60-kg bags up from 353,960 bags shipped the previous month. Exports in December were spurred by the removal of a coffee tax and the high level of beginning stocks. The November figure was well below a provisional estimate of 436,261 bags but slightly up on 340,000 bags sold in October.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala exported 443,155 60-kg bags of coffee in December 1996, up 43 per cent from the 310,546 bags shipped the same month the previous year, the National Coffee Association (ANACAFE) said. The Association added that the high exports were due to favourable prices not to a larger harvest. In November the Association put 1996/97 (October/September) production at 3.45 to 3.60 million 60-kg bags compared to the 3.6 million bags produced in 1995/96.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.388 million bags of coffee in October 1996, 3 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 15.860 million bags, 15 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 increased by 5.8 per cent to 17.1 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Guatemala (1.308 vs 1.313 million bags), Mexico (3.225 vs 2.366 million bags), Brazil (1.305 vs 2.079 million bags) and Colombia (2.399 vs 1.909 million bags). The country exported 1.715 million bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 19 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell by 22 per cent to 1.841 million bags.
